In a broad bipartisan vote, the Senate passed a Medicare reform bill that provides a permanent solution to the "doc fix" and extends a popular children's health insurance program. The legislation, which now heads to President Obama for signature, aims to stabilize physician payments and prevent imminent reimbursement cuts. While the bill passed with 92 votes, some conservative senators opposed it due to concerns over its long-term cost and impact on the national debt.

The White House argues it can bypass congressional approval for the Iran nuclear deal, but historical precedent suggests securing legislative consent would make the agreement far more durable. While the administration frames the deal as a nonbinding executive agreement to avoid political gridlock, the push for congressional review—exemplified by the Corker bill—highlights the significant political risks of sidestepping the legislative branch. Ultimately, moving forward without Congress risks creating a less stable diplomatic breakthrough that could face legal challenges and lack the enduring legitimacy of a treaty ratified by the Senate.

A bystander's cell phone video contradicted the initial police report, showing North Charleston officer Michael Slager shooting unarmed Walter Scott in the back as he fled. Slager has been fired and charged with murder, while the witness who recorded the footage stated he did not see Scott grab the officer's Taser.

In a lighthearted exchange in Japan's parliament, Defense Minister Gen Nakatani assured lawmakers that the Air Self Defense Force has never encountered a UFO, responding to a query from flamboyant politician Antonio Inoki. Inoki, a former wrestler who has pushed for "basketball diplomacy" and claimed to have seen a UFO, asked if Japan had protocols for extraterrestrial threats. While Nakatani clarified that jets are scrambled for unidentified objects—often identifying them as birds—he confirmed there is no record of alien visitations.

The Department of Defense announced that the remains of nearly 400 unidentified service members from the USS Oklahoma will be been exhumed later this year. These sailors and Marines were lost during the December 7, 1s 1941, attack on Pearl Harbor, and will finally be identified and returned to their families with full military honors.

Kayahan, one of Turkey’s most beloved singers and songwriters, has died of cancer at the age of 66 in Istanbul. Diagnosed with the disease in 1990, he battled recurrent cancer over the decades while achieving significant fame, particularly with his 1991 album "I Made a Vow." Tributes from figures such as Prime Minister Ahmet Davutoglu highlight his lasting impact on Turkish music through his countless compositions and distinctive tenor voice.

The Pentagon released a map showing significant territorial gains against ISIS in Iraq, though experts cautioned that the battle lines may fluctuate due to the nature of asymmetric warfare. Specialist Afzal Ashraf explains that while the coalition is making progress, ISIS is using a strategy of withdrawing from front lines to maintain their image of strength through spectacular attacks.

Intense fighting and Saudi-led coalition airstrikes in Yemen have killed approximately 600 people in less than two weeks, causing widespread destruction and leaving millions without electricity. As the humanitarian crisis worsens, the International Committee of the Red Cross is calling for an immediate ceasefire to deliver life-saving medical supplies to the region. While the U.N. Security Council has discussed the situation, political efforts to resolve the conflict remain stalled.

As ISIS militants targeted the Yazidi community to justify sexual slavery, many women and young girls were forcibly captured and held in "warehouses" to be distributed among fighters. The article follows the harrowing account of 19-year-old Hanan, who survived being held as a sex slave by escaping through a window during a desperate attempt to flee. Though she is physically free, Hanan remains deeply traumatized by the violence and terror she endured.

HLN's #MeForReal campaign encourages people to share unfiltered, real-life moments to combat online judgment, sparked by singer P!nk's positive response to body-shaming comments about her post-cancer benefit photo. The article highlights how P!nk's confident rebuttal inspired fans to embrace their own "squishiness" and imperfections, ultimately turning the haters' negativity into more support for the artist.

Three weeks into Saudi Arabia’s airstrikes against Houthi rebels in Yemen, the conflict shows no signs of easing, with civilian casualties mounting and thousands fleeing across the Red Sea. As the death toll rises, fears are growing that the violence is part of a broader proxy war between Saudi Arabia and Iran for regional dominance. Meanwhile, the UN Security Council has approved an arms embargo and sanctions against the Houthis, aiming to curb the violence and limit the spread of terrorism.

After a flight from Abu Dhabi to New York, American traveler Jennifer Stewart’s two-year-old cat, Felix, went missing due to a damaged carrier. Etihad Airways is currently investigating the incident and working with ground handlers to locate the pet, while Stewart expressed devastation over the airline's handling of the live animal. The airline stated that while such losses are extremely rare, they are reviewing their pet handling procedures to prevent future occurrences.

Canadian actor Jonathan Crombie, best known for his role as Gilbert Blythe in the beloved "Anne of Green Gables" television movies, has died at the age of 48 due to complications from a brain hemorrhage. Producer Kevin Sullivan remembered Crombie as a dedicated actor who brought significant chemistry and heart to the iconic series, which became a cultural touchstone in Canada and internationally. While Crombie appeared in other productions, he remained deeply proud of his portrayal of Gilbert Blythe, a role that earned him a lasting legacy and affection from fans worldwide.

Thai Smile, a subsidiary of Thai Airways, unveiled a new themed Airbus A20 aircraft featuring the characters from the hit Cartoon Network show, *Adventure Time*. The partnership between Thai Smile and Cartoon Network aims to bring the show's psychedelic aesthetic to the skies, with themed interior amenities and colorful new livery. The inaugural flight is scheduled to depart from Bangkok to Phuket on April 4.

The California Department of Public Health declared that the measles outbreak involving over 130 cases is now over, 42 days after the last known case of the B3 strain. The health department credited prompt investigation, contact tracing, and vaccination efforts for controlling the outbreak, which initially stemmed from visitors to two Disney theme parks. The remaining five cases involved a different measles genotype, and health officials continue to monitor the situation for any new occurrences.

Robert Bates, the Oklahoma deputy accused of manslaughter, defended his claim that he mistook a pistol for a stun gun during a fatal shooting with suspect Eric Harris. Amidst the investigation, allegations have surfaced that the sheriff's office may have falsified Bates' training records to meet requirements for his advanced deputy status.

After a two-year shutdown, the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) has successfully restarted its particle beams at CERN. This massive physics experiment aims to recreate conditions from the Big Bang to better understand the origins of the universe and the fundamental forces of nature. Scientists hope these experiments will provide answers to long-standing mysteries, such as the nature of dark matter and the origin of mass.

While traveling through a rainy Washington, D.C., a group of pedestrians and restaurant patrons worked together to help a mother duck and her ducklings safely cross a busy street. The group used an umbrella to guide the birds and stopped traffic to ensure they reached a safer, grassy area.

As the fight against ISIS intensifies, Western military veterans are increasingly traveling to the Middle East to serve as volunteer trainers for local forces. While some fighters join militias like the YPG to engage in combat, others focus on providing specialized expertise to support regional troops. However, these foreign volunteers face mixed receptions, as some local groups prefer to fight independently to maintain national pride.

To enforce a recent ban on beef, police in Malegaon, India, are requiring residents to submit "mugshots" and detailed physical descriptions of their cattle to create a tracking database. This measure aims to prevent illegal cow slaughter, which is a highly sensitive issue due to the religious significance of cattle to the Hindu majority. While many owners have complied, the decision has faced backlash from beef traders and critics who argue against government interference in personal dietary choices.

Avril Lavigne has revealed that her recent absence from the music scene was due to a severe battle with Lyme disease that left her bedridden for five months. The singer, who is now feeling much better, shared that the illness was a life-changing experience that has given her a new perspective on enjoying life.

Deion Sanders publicly scolded his son, Deion Sanders Jr., on Twitter for eating "hood doughnuts," reminding him he has a trust fund, a condo, and his own clothing line. The elder Sanders emphasized that his son, who attends Southern Methodist University, should act like a "Huxtable" rather than embrace street culture. Junior took the teasing in stride by retweeting his father's comments, which also referenced luxury brands like Versace.

Bob Barker, the former host of "The Price Is Right" for 35 years, returned to the show for its April 1 episode after a 8-year hiatus. The 91-year-old TV legend hosted the "Lucky Seven" segment before handing duties back to current host Drew Carey. Despite his long absence, Barker appeared sharp and did not seem to miss a beat.

An explosion at a paraxylene chemical plant in Fujian province, China, left six people injured and sparked a large fire. The blast, which occurred at an oil storage facility, was reportedly caused by an oil leak, and the fire has since been brought under control by over 600 firefighters. The incident has reignited concerns over the plant's history of protests and its relocation from a densely populated area due to pollution risks.

California's ongoing drought threatens national food prices, as the state supplies over a third of the nation's produce. The 2015 MTV Movie Awards hosted Amy Schumer, featuring a mix of hilarious hits and awkward misfires. Highlights included Channing Tatum’s twerking for Jennifer Lopez and Kevin Hart’s heartwarming family moment, while Schumer’s archery-themed gag and controversial jokes were criticized as misses.

Easter is a complex Christian holiday rooted in the Crucifixion and Resurrection of Jesus, yet it is surrounded by secular traditions like bunnies and eggs, as well as astronomical factors that determine its shifting date. The article explores the religious significance of Holy Week, highlighting recent celebrations at the Vatican and in Jerusalem, while noting the date discrepancy between Western and Eastern Orthodox calendars. It also addresses the coincidence of a recent blood moon occurring near Easter and explains the cosmic rules governing the holiday's timing.

Italian photographer Carolina Sandretto captures the intimate, communal life within Cuba's crumbling "solares," where multiple generations share living in single-family dwellings. Her work explores the unique social dynamics of these crowded homes, which were a result of historical housing redistributions and the need to accommodate growing populations. As diplomatic relations between the U own and Cuba thaw, Sandretto aims to document how these traditional, much-layered habitats might change due to an influx of visitors and modern technology.

Abdirahman Sheik Mohamud, a 23-year-old naturalized U.S. citizen, pleaded not guilty in Ohio to federal charges of providing material support to terrorists and lying to the FBI. Prosecutors allege that Mohamud traveled to Syria in 2014 for terrorist training and planned to return to the United States to carry out execution-style attacks against U.S. soldiers.

NBA player Thabo Sefolosha claims that his season-ending leg injury was caused by police during his arrest, which he and teammate Pero Antic were charged with misdemeanors after being found near the scene of a stabbing. The New York Police Department has opened an Internal Affairs Bureau investigation into the incident. Sefolosha, who suffered a fractured fibula and ligament damage, will undergo surgery and miss the rest of the season, including the playoffs, which begin this weekend. The Hawks enter as the top seed in the NBA's Eastern Conference.

"Grace of Monaco," starring Nicole Kidman, is heading to Lifetime for a Memorial Day premiere after The Weinstein Company sold the U.S. distribution rights following poor international reception and critical pans. The film, which focuses on Princess Grace Kelly's 1962 tax dispute with France, was originally positioned as an awards contender but was pulled from theatrical release due to creative disputes between director Olivier Dahan and Harvey Weinstein.

A naturalized U.S. citizen from Columbus was arrested and pleaded not guilty to charges of providing material support to terrorists and lying to the FBI. The 23-year-old allegedly traveled to Syria for training with the intent to return home and kill Americans, particularly U.S. soldiers, execution style.

Turkish authorities arrested nine British citizens, including four children, for attempting crossing illegally into Syria. The Turkish military stated that the group was trying to get into Syria, which has been torn by a roughly four-year war between Syrian government forces and Islamist extremist groups and other rebels. Among the war's combatants is ISIS, which has taken over parts of Syria and Iraq for what it claims is its Islamic caliphate, and which is known to have been recruiting Westerners.

A high-speed driving experience at Walt Disney World Speedway turned fatal on Sunday when a Lamborghini crashed into a guardrail. The passenger, 36-year-old Gary Terry, died at the scene, while the 24-year-old driver was hospitalized with minor injuries.

Executive producer Brian Grazer announced that the series *Arrested Development* will return for a fifth season consisting of 17 episodes. While Netflix has not officially commented, the news provides relief to a devoted fanbase waiting to see if the original cast will return.

A massive fire on a Pemex oil rig off the coast of Mexico resulted in four deaths and injured 45 workers, with two remaining in serious condition. Authorities successfully evacuated approximately 300 people and extinguished the blaze by Wednesday night, while denying reports of a platform collapse or oil spill. The specific cause of the fire, which started in the platform's dehydration and pumping area, has not yet been determined.

Pemex, the state oil company, confirmed that the blaze was extingued by Wednesday night after authorities evacuated approximately 300 people and deployed ten boats to fight the flames. The company stated there was no oil spill and denied rumors that the platform had collapsed, while the cause of the fire remains under investigation.

A nuclear submarine undergoing repairs at the Zvezodochka shipyard in northwestern Russia caught fire on Tuesday, reportedly caused by spanners' welding work. The fire was extinguished without causing any injuries, and authorities confirmed the vessel's nuclear reactor had been unloaded and posed no threat to the public population.

Both men relied on ingenuity and resourcefulness to survive until they were spotted by passing ships.

A Saudi official reported that more than 500 Houthi rebels have been killed and 1,200 airstrikes conducted since the start of the Saudi-led military campaign in Yemen. The conflict has resulted in significant casualties on both sides, with three Saudi officers killed in border clashes and hundreds of Yemeni civilians reported dead or wounded. Meanwhile, the UN highlights that the ongoing chaos has left most of Yemen's population in need of humanitarian assistance.

This shift is attributed to the group's significant weakening in Somalia due to sustained pressure from African Union forces and U.S. drone and special operations campaigns that have decimated their leadership and territorial control. Consequently, the attack serves as a desperate attempt by an unraveling organization to maintain relevance despite its declining capabilities.

ISIS affiliate Ansar Beit Al-Maqdis claimed responsibility for two of the blasts, which occurred near a police station and on a highway, while a third shooting incident left three security personnel injured. These attacks coincide with a recent reshuffle of senior military leadership in Egypt as the army continues its decade-long counter operation against insurgents in the area.

ABC is developing a revival of "The Muppets" with Bill Prady co-writing the script, aiming for a May upfront presentation. A one-year-old dog named Theia survived being hit by a car, struck with a hammer, and buried in a field, only to stagger to a nearby farm four days later. Now receiving extensive medical care at Washington State University, the injured but gentle dog has inspired a successful fundraising campaign that has already surpassed its $10,000 goal to cover her ongoing treatment. Her foster owner, Sara Mellado, is dedicated to finding Theia a loving home and plans to donate any excess funds to help other animals.

Kim Ki-Jong has been charged with attempted murder following the stabbing of U.S. Ambassador Mark Lippert during a recent event in Seoul. The suspect allegedly attacked the ambassador over opposition to joint military drills and is currently under investigation for potential ties to North Korea. President Park Geun-hye condemned the attack, stating it was an assault on the alliance between South Korea and the United States.

Michelle MacLaren has departed as director of the upcoming "Wonder Woman" film, citing "creative differences" with Warner Bros. Pictures. The report comes from The Hollywood Reporter, confirming that the movie, starring Gal Gadot as the Amazon princess, remains slued for a June 23, 2017 release. Warner Bros. now needs to find a new director for the project.

Robert Lewis Burns Jr., the original drummer for Southern rock band Lynyrd Skynyrd, died at age 64 in a single-vehicle car crash in Georgia. Burns, who left the band in 1975, was not wearing a seatbelt when his car struck a mailbox and a tree shortly before midnight. Fellow original member Gary Rossington paid tribute to Burns, remembering him as a "funny guy" and a "great great drummer."

This article highlights several highly anticipated television premieres and season returns scheduled for the week of April 18. It provides insights into upcoming plots and cast developments for shows such as *Orphan Black*, *Turn: Washington's Spies*, and *Game of Thrones*.

After facing professional setbacks, entrepreneur Jia Jiang launched the "100 Days of Rejection" project to confront his fear of being told "no" and demystify the experience. Cuba has returned to the Summit of the Americas for the first time since 1962, marking a significant diplomatic shift as the United States no longer blocks its participation. Authorities reported that the attacks in Durban killed two immigrants and three South Africans, including a 14-year-old boy, as heavily armed police scrambled to stop clashes after local residents accused immigrants of taking their jobs. Recent statistics show that 8 out of 10 American taxpayers receive a refund averaging around $3,000, making tax season a "happy spending spree" despite the system's inherent complexities and biases. While the process has been simplified by free filing software, the article notes that the tax code remains biased against two-worker marriages and the wealthy, who benefit from untaxed capital gains.

Mark Wahlberg is set to star in and produce a new film titled "Patriots' Day," which will depict the Boston Marathon bombing and the subsequent manhunt from the perspective of Police Commissioner Ed Davis. The project, produced by CBS Films, will incorporate research and footage from the "60 Minutes" news program. This announcement comes alongside another upcoming film about the event titled "Boston Strong."

These personal tragedies serve to strengthen the resolve of the international community to end hostilities and provide essential aid to vulnerable civilians.

Ultimately, the author argues that political will must be exerted to ensure safe humanitarian access and to protect the thousands of lives caught in the Syrian conflict.

A 21-year-old man with cerebral cerebral palsy was found abandoned in a Philadelphia park for over four days, allegedly left there by his mother, who fled to Maryland. The mother now faces charges of aggravated assault and kidnapping after police located her following a tip from family members. The man was rescued and hospitalized for malnutrition and dehydration, while the mother was taken into custody by Maryland police.

As the fifth season of *Game of Thrones* begins, the series aims to build a dramatic crescendo with larger-scale battles and major story arcs moving into the next phase. 

The upcoming season will see characters like Tyrion, Daenerys, and the Stark daughters face shifting political roles and colliding paths. 

As the show reaches its halfway point, the narrative will focus on the consequences of war and the growing tension between the nobility and the suffering common folk.

Five Chinese feminists face up to five years in prison after being detained for organizing gender equality campaigns and International Women's Day protests. The activists, members of the Women's Rights Action Group, face charges of "disturbing public order," a move that has drawn international condemnation from human rights groups and political figures.

Multiple powerful tornadoes across the rural Midwest on Thursday, including Illinois, Iowa, and Oklahoma, resulted in one death and numerous injuries, but widespread damage to homes and businesses. The storms carved paths through several communities, destroying structures and up trees, yet officials noted that the overall casualty count remained surprisingly low given the severity of the destruction.

Chris Copeland of the Indiana Pacers was stabbed after leaving a New York nightclub early Wednesday, and two Atlanta Hawks -- who had just finished a home game hours before the incident -- were among those arrested, according to police and CNN affiliates. The Hawks were not involved in the stabbing incident, police said, but were arrested on obstruction and other charges later.

Three weeks into Saudi-led airstrikes against Houthi rebels, the conflict in Yemen shows no signs of slowing, resulting in mounting civilian casualties and a growing refugee crisis. The fighting has intensified fears of a proxy war between Saudi Arabia and Iran for regional dominance, as the Houthis continue to hold significant territory. While the U.N. Security Council has passed an arms embargo to curb the violence, the humanitarian situation remains dire.

HLN’s #MeForReal campaign encourages users to share unfiltered, authentic moments online to counteract the judgment often found on social media. This initiative gained momentum when singer P!nk responded to body-shaming comments about her appearance by embracing her "squishiness," which inspired her fans to do the same. Ultimately, the campaign highlights the value of self-acceptance and challenges the internet culture of perfectionism.

A Los Angeles judge has ordered V. Stiviano to repay more than $2.6 million in luxury gifts provided to her by former Clippers owner Donald Sterling. The ruling follows a lawsuit by Sterling's wife, Shelly, who successfully argued that the assets were community property intended to be recovered by the injured spouse.

Emmy-winning actor Richard Dysart has died at the age of 86 following a long illness. He was best known for his portrayal of senior partner Leland McKenzie on the long-running NBC drama *L.A. Law*, a role for which he won an Emmy in 1992.

Following a deadly massacre at a university in Garissa, Kenyan authorities have identified several local individuals as suspected perpetrators of the Al-Shabaab-linked attack. The government is now grappling with the realization that the terror group is successfully recruiting disaffected Kenyan youth from within their own communities. This surge in homegrown radicalization has left the nation facing the difficult task of countering terrorists who are deeply embedded in local society.

Former Congress Michele Bachmann has been facing widespread criticism after she compared President Obama to the co-pilot of the doomed Germanwings flight, in a Facebook comment posted March 31. Bachmann’s post was widely criticized, with many calling it moronic and despicable. Bachmann is no stranger to voicing her opinion on the President's dealing with Iran, personally telling him to "bomb Iran" during the 2014 White House Christmas Party.

National Park Week, running from April 18 to 26, offers free admission to the 128 U.S. national parks that typically charge fees, including popular sites like Yellowstone and Yosemite. The initiative, hosted by the National Park Service and the National Park Foundation, features events like astronomy parties and Junior Ranger activities, with more information available at FindYourPark.com. The campaign encourages visitors to explore and share their experiences using the hashtag #FindYourPark.

An independent review by Columbia Journalism School professors concluded that Rolling Stone suffered an "institutional failure" in its reporting and editing of a deeply flawed article regarding a purported gang rape at the University of Virginia. In response, the magazine’s managing editor issued an apology to readers and those affected by the story, while legal experts note that fraternity members may pursue defamation lawsuits against the publication. However, such legal action faces significant hurdles, as the university itself cannot sue for defamation, and fraternities must prove that the false statements specifically concerned them and caused reputational harm.

A Duke University student admitted to hanging a noose near a student union, sparking protests and a forum where the president condemned the "cowardly act." The incident is part of a broader pattern of racist events on campuses, including a recent case at the University of Oklahoma where students were expelled for using racial slurs. University officials are conducting a student conduct review and ongoing criminal investigations into the noose hanging.

The ongoing California drought, which has prompted mandatory water cuts, threatens to raise grocery prices for fruits, vegetables, and dairy because the state produces a significant portion of the nation's produce. While a strong dollar and lower oil prices may help mitigate these costs by facilitating imports and reducing transportation expenses, experts warn that farmers' planting decisions could still lead to higher supermarket prices. Additionally, severe drought conditions in Texas and Oklahoma have already driven up beef and veal costs, highlighting a broader regional impact on food availability and pricing.

Robert Bates' lawyer released training documents to verify the reserve deputy's qualifications in the fatal shooting of Eric Harris. The records show Bates completed minimal Taser and firearms training, though his attorney claims he met all state requirements. The documents have become central to the case, as the victim's family alleges Bates received preferential treatment due to donations and personal connections.

The historic California drought, which is affecting the nation's food supply, has prompting Governor Jerry Brown to implement mandatory water usage cuts. Because California produces a vast portion of the country's produce, experts warn that the shortage could lead to significant price increases for fruits and vegetables.

While the strength of the dollar and lower oil prices may offset some costs, economists remain uncertain about how much the drought will impact grocery prices and farming decisions.

The UN Security Council voted in favor of an arms embargo against the Houthi group, which has taken over large swaths of Yemen, including its capital, Sanaa, and supporters of former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. The resolution "raises the cost" for the Houthis, according to Mark Lyall Grant, Britain's ambassador to the United Nations. In addition to the arms embargo, it also demands that the Shiite group pull back and refrain from more violence and includes sanctions aimed to controlling the spread of terrorism, according to Grant. Former rap mogul Marion "Suge" Knight has been ordered to stand trial for murder, attempted murder, and hit-and-run charges following a deadly incident on the set of "Straight Outta Compton." During the preliminary hearing, Judge Ronald Coen lowered Knight's bail to $10 million and dismissed one of the hit-and-run counts, citing legal restrictions on multiple charges involving the same vehicle. Knight faces up to life in prison if convicted, while the sole surviving victim, Cle Sloan, has refused to testify against him despite prosecutors offering immunity.

Liana Barrientos, 39, is facing criminal charges after allegedly entering into ten different marriages as part of an immigration scam to help her husbands obtain permanent residency. Prosecutors claim that Barrientos often married multiple men within short timeframes, only divorcing them after their residency status was secured. She has pleaded not guilty to the charges and faces up to four years in prison if convicted.

Jodi Arias was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of early release for the 2018 murder of Travis Alexander. Despite the prosecution's pursuit of the death penalty, the jury failed to reach a unanimous decision, leaving the sentencing decision for the judge, who ultimately opted for life imprisonment. Arias, who expressed remorse and disgust regarding her actions, will serve her sentence at the Lumley Unit in the Arizona State Prison Complex-Perryville near Goodyear.

A third suspect, George Davon Kennedy, has been arrested in connection with a widely publicized gang rape that was filmed on a crowded Panama City Beach. This arrest follows the previous detentions of Ryan Calhoun and Delonte Martistee, both of whom are students at Troy University. Authorities are continuing to investigate the incident, which occurred in broad daylight while bystanders watched.

A New York judge recently authorized serving divorce papers on a husband via Facebook, which has sparked a discussion about the modernization of legal service of process. The article explains that traditional methods like in-person service, mail, and posting notices in obscure publications are often unreliable when dealing with defendants who actively avoid legal notice. The ruling suggests that using social media may be a more effective way to ensure defendants are properly notified of lawsuits than these outdated alternatives.

A new study suggests that "Double Falsehood," attributed to Lewis Theobald, was actually co-written by Shakespeare himself with help from his friend John Fletcher. Using computer software to analyze word choices and phrase patterns, researchers Ryan L. Boyd and James W. Pennebaker determined that the play's first half was almost entirely written by Shakespeare, while the second half appeared to be split evenly between the two. The findings, published in Psychological Science, settle a long-standing literary debate regarding the play's authorship.

Reserve Deputy Robert Bates turned himself in to authorities on Tuesday after being charged with second-degree manslaughter for the fatal shooting of Eric Courtney Harris. While Bates claims he inadvertently fired his handgun instead of a Taser during an undercover sting, the victim's family and legal counsel are calling the shooting an act of unjustified brutality. Bates has since posted $25,000 bail and maintains his innocence.

Kanye West has reached a settlement with paparazzi photographer Daniel Ramos following an altercation at Los Angeles International Airport in 2013. The case, which involved West pleading no contest to a misdemeanor count of battery, concluded with a judge ordering two years' probation and anger management sessions. The legal team emphasized the settlement was a victory for Ramos, highlighting that West issued a public apology and acknowledged the celebrities have no right to physically assault someone simply because they were asked a question.

Robert Bates, a reserve deputy charged in the death of Eric Harris, claims he accidentally shot Harris while reaching for his Taser, stating "it can happen to anyone." Despite Bates asserting he completed required training, the sheriff's office cannot locate his firearms certification records, and officials are investigating allegations that his training records were forged.

An Alaska Airlines flight was forced to make an emergency landing after passengers heard banging and yelling from the cargo hold, revealing that a ramp agent had fallen asleep inside. The plane, which had only been airborne for 14 minutes, returned to Seattle-Tacoma International Airport where the employee was found unharmed and subsequently discharged from a hospital. Alaska Airlines is currently investigating the incident, noting that the worker was missing from a pre-departure huddle and his colleagues mistakenly assumed he had gone home.

Swedish photographer Johan Bavman documents the experience of fathers utilizing the generous 480-day parental leave system, where mothers and fathers can share leave to care for newborns. The program mandates "daddy months" to promote shared parenting, though only 12% of couples currently equally share the leave. Bavman aims to photograph 60 fathers to highlight the struggles and joys of modern parenthood.

To kick off peak season, 7-Eleven is hosting its first "Bring-Your-Own-Cup" Slurpee Day this Saturday from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Customers can fill any sanitary, creative vessel—such as a trophy or sand bucket—for the price of a medium Slurpee ($1.49). While the promotion encourages unique containers, items must fit through a 10-inch diameter hole to ensure they are practical for consumption.

This week's entertainment news was dominated by major announcements: "Star Wars" became available for digital streaming, "The Vampire Diaries" star Nina Dobrev exited the series causing a fan uproar, and Mindy Kaling's brother revealed he faked being Black to gain medical school admission. Additionally, Burger King celebrated a couple's fast-food-themed wedding, and Michelle Obama showcased her dancing skills during the White House Easter egg roll.

As tropical storm Maysak (known locally as Chedeng) approaches the Philippines, authorities have issued warnings for flash floods and landslides while implementing preemptive evacuations and travel restrictions. Although the storm has weakened from super typhoon status, officials are urging residents to prepare for significant impact as it approaches landfall in Isabela province.

T Tulsa County reserve deputy Robert Bates turned to authorities and charged second-degree manslaughter for the fatal shooting of Eric Courtney Harris during an undercover weapons sting. Bates surrendered, while his attorney maintains that the shooting was an "excusable homicide" and argues that the charge is unwarrant. The Harris family has welcomed the charges but is demanding an independent investigation, questioning why a 73-year-old volunteer deputy was involved in such a high-risk operation.

The Boston Marathon bombing suspect, Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, was found guilty on all counts following two days of jury deliberation. The verdict was predictable, but the greater significance lies in understanding how radicalization drives such violence, as attackers often stem from community grievances and perceived injustices rather than inherent predisposition. The article further explores how geopolitical conflicts and religious identity intersections frequently radicalize young Muslims, suggesting that preventing future attacks requires a deeper understanding of these drivers rather than mere assumption.

An Amnesty International report highlights the growing number of attacks on women's rights activists in Afghanistan, noting that perpetrators often remain alive due to insufficient government action. The report examines how both the Taliban and government officials contribute to a climate of danger, following the brutal murder of activist Farkhunda. Despite these rising risks and increasing violence, female activists continue to demonstrate remarkable resilience through acts of solidarity.

Trey Moses, a star high school basketball recruit, surprised freshman Ellie Meredith by asking her to be his prom date in a viral "prom-posal." The gesture highlights the inclusive environment of their school's Best Buddies program, which fosters friendships between students with and without developmental disabilities. Beyond the social impact, Trey plans to study special education in college to continue his commitment to helping others.

Hundreds of additional Iraqi troops, including federal police and militia members, have been deployed to reinforce forces defending the strategic Baiji oil refinery against an ongoing ISIS assault. Although ISIS claimed to have taken control of parts of the facility, Iraqi officials maintain that their troops are holding their ground and preparing to repel the attackers. This reinforcement effort aims to protect a critical source of domestic fuel and prevent significant damage to Iraq's oil infrastructure.

Andrew Getty, the 47-year-old heir to the billion-dollar oil fortune, has died following natural causes at his home. The Los Angeles Police Department confirmed that there was no foul play involved in his death, noting that the coroner's office is investigating his medical history and the presence of medication found at the scene.

Severe weather struck the Midwest on Wednesday night, with tornadoes reported in Kansas and Missouri, including one near Goddard and another in Potosi. Chad Myers warned that nighttime tornadoes are particularly dangerous, and additional storms are expected across the Midwest and South on Thursday.

FBI agents and task force officers were following 36-year-old Kevone Charleston of Austell, Georgia, as he pulled into a CVS pharmacy in Forsyth County, Georgia, early Saturday. Charleston is suspected of involvement in 32 commercial robberies dating to November 2013, according to FBI officials. During the incident, two FBI agents were injured when Charleston fled in his vehicle, collided with government vehicles, and was subsequently shot and wounded by agents before being captured.

ISIS claimed to have seized control of parts of Iraq's largest oil refinery following an assault on Saturday, though Iraqi government officials denied the claim and insisted they maintain full control. The strategic facility remains a highly contested target due to its importance to Iraq's domestic fuel supply and its proximity to the recently liberated city of Tikrit.

Liana Barrientos, 39, was arrested and charged with offering a false instrument for filing after she married 10 times in under two decades, primarily to secure immigration status. Prosecutors allege the marriages were part of an immigration scam, with many occurring in quick succession across locations like Westchester and the Bronx. Barrientos pleaded not guilty at State Supreme Court and faces up to four years in prison if convicted, with her next court appearance scheduled for May 18.

Tulsa County reserve deputy Robert Bates turned himself in and posted bail after being charged with second-degree manslaughter for fatally shooting Eric Courtney Harris during an undercover sting operation. While authorities claim Bates inadvertently fired his gun instead of deploying his Taser, Harris’s family and attorneys argue that excessive force was unnecessary and have called for an independent investigation into the incident. The case has sparked public criticism regarding the involvement of a volunteer reserve deputy with significant financial ties to the sheriff's office.

A resiliently surviving stray dog named Theia has survived multiple life-threatening incidents, including being hit by a car, a botched mercy killing, and being buried in a field. 

Theia is currently receiving specialized veterinary care for severe injuries, while her owner has launched fundraising efforts to support her ongoing medical needs.

Despite suffering severe injuries, including a dislocated jaw and sinus damage, the "miracle dog" has inspired supporters to raise over $10,000 for her medical care. Her foster parent, Sara Mellado, is working to ensure she receives necessary surgeries before being placed in a loving, permanent home.

A faulty electrical cable caused explosions at the University of Nairobi's Kikuyu campus, leading to panic and stampedes that resulted in one death and dozens of injuries.

The incident occurred amid heightened fears of terrorist attacks following a recent massacre in Garissa, prompting authorities to investigate the electrical failure.

The university has called for calm as officials work to repair the equipment and medical teams treat the injured.

Richie Benaud, the legendary Australian cricketer and broadcaster, passed away at the age of 84. He was remembered as one of the greatest all-rounders in the game, famed for his witty one-liners and his record-breaking leg-spinner, and his voice was described as the "soundboard to an Australian summer." His passing generated a wave of condolences across the cricketing world, including from Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott, who said Benaud personified the traditions and values of the sport.

Consequently, the author advocates for the widespread deployment of police body cameras to ensure accountability, deter excessive force, and help rebuild public trust in law enforcement.

Investigators in Marseille have successfully collected all main evidence from the Germanwings Flight 9525 crash site, leaving the investigators to stay with a private security firm to secure remaining debris. 

The investigation revealed that the co-pilot, Andreas Lubitz, intentionally engineered the plane's demise by manipulating controls to accelerate the descent. Authorities believe the crash, which killed all 150 people on board, was caused by Lubitz's actions following years of battling depression and concealing his medical leave.

Blue Bell has temporarily closed its Broken Arrow facility in Oklahoma after discovering Listeria contamination in ice cream served there. Health officials warn consumers not to eat products marked with specific letters, as the company recalls affected items to investigate the outbreak that has hospitalized five people in Kansas. The CDC advises checking freezers and throwing away any recalled 3-ounce servings immediately.

Kansas has enacted the first U.S. law banning "dismemberment" abortion procedures, which are commonly used in the second trimester. The law, signed by Governor Sam Brownback, allows exceptions only to protect the mother's life or health and is the most restrictive abortion ban in the country. Supporters view it as a landmark victory for the pro-life movement, while opponents argue it endangers women's health and plan to challenge it in court.

Legendary Australian cricket captain and iconic broadcaster Richie Benaud has died at the age of 84. Celebrated for his record-breaking playing career and his witty commentary, Benaud was revered globally as one of the most influential figures in the history of the sport.

During a recent episode of "The Price Is Right," model Manuela Arbelaez accidentally revealed the correct price of a new car, much to the amusement of host Drew Carey. Although the mistake left Arbelaez mortified, the mishap was handled with humor and she later confirmed everything was fine.

One year after the kidnapping of nearly 300 schoolgirls by Boko Haram in Nigeria, President-elect Muhammadu Buhari marked the anniversary with a call to reflect on the suffering of the victims and their families. The incident sparked global outrage and the "Bring Back Our Girls" campaign, while hundreds of the abducted girls still remain missing. The tragedy has resulted in significant political changes, including the defeat of President Goodluck Jonathan, who was criticized for his handling of the security crisis, and the rise of Buhari, who has pledged a stronger military effort against the militant group.

Australian Prime Minister Tony Abbott has announced a "no jab, no pay" policy that will remove conscientious objector exemptions for parents who refuse to vaccinate their children. Under this new policy, starting in January 2016, families who opt out of vaccinations could lose up to $11,000 in annual child care benefits. While medical and religious exemptions will remain, the government aims to tighten guidelines to ensure taxpayer-funded benefits support public health goals.

Chris Rock has sparked renewed conversation about racial disparities in policing by documenting three traffic stops in seven weeks on Twitter, drawing both support and criticism. His posts come amid heightened sensitivity following high-profile deaths like Eric Garner and Michael Brown, and he previously advised comedian Jerry Seinfeld that having a white friend in the car can help avoid police trouble. Actor Isaiah Washington suggested Rock adapt by switching to less conspicuous cars to avoid being pulled over, highlighting the ongoing tension between documenting racial profiling and the pressure to change one's behavior to avoid it.

Universal's *Furious 7* is projected to have a massive weekend debut of up to $138 million, marking the largest North American opening since late 2013. Driven by the popularity of the franchise and the late Paul Walker, the film is poised to become the biggest opening of 2015 with a massive global release.

A Philadelphia woman faces multiple charges after allegedly abandoning her 21-year-old quadriplegic son in a park for four days to visit a boyfriend in Maryland. The victim, who suffers from cerebral palsy, was found in harsh weather conditions and is being treated for dehydration, malnutrition, and other injuries. The mother was taken into custody in Maryland and will face extradition to Philadelphia to answer for the charges.

The California Public Utilities Commission ordered Pacific Gas & Electric to pay a record $1.6 billion penalty for unsafe operations, including the 2010 San Bruno pipeline explosion that killed eight people. Most of the funds will be directed toward gas transmission pipeline safety improvements and other remedies to prevent future incidents. PG&E's CEO stated the company is dedicated to re-earning public trust and implementing safety upgrades following the tragedy.

Mary Kay Letourneau and her husband, Vili Fualaau, are set to appear on ABC's "20/20" to discuss their enduring marriage and upcoming 10th wedding anniversary, despite the controversy surrounding their relationship that originally led to Letourneau's imprisonment. Elizabeth Sedway was removed from an Alaska Airlines flight from Hawaii to San Jose, California, after she repeatedly to the crew that she had cancer, despite the crew's concern for her well-being. Sedway was eventually allowed to board a later flight, but she missed her chemotherapy and her family incurred significant disruptions. The airline has since apologized and refunded her tickets.

A Rolling Stone article about a sexual assault at a University of Virginia campus was to be retracted after a Columbia University investigation found "journalistic malpractice," including errors in reporting, editing, and fact-checking. Sabrina Rubin Erdely never verified her attacker's identity or gave the fraternity a fair chance to respond. The story's pull from the magazine's website followed 2.7 million hits and sparked a nationwide debate about campus sexual violence.

Pope Francis commemorated the Armenian genocide by quoting Pope John Paul II’s 1001 document, which explicitly used the term "genocide," thereby honoring continuity over diplomatic deference. The Pope’s carefully crafted phrasing avoided the "g-word" to maintain Vatican stability, despite pressure from analysts who warned that silence would signal a policy shift.

Hillary Clinton officially launched her 2016 presidential campaign, leveraging her extensive experience and name recognition to position herself as a strong Democratic contender. However, she faces the challenge of avoiding the "inauthentic" image that plagued Al Gore, needing to present a compelling vision rather than relying on the perception of inevitability. To counter doubts about her trustworthiness, her campaign is shifting focus to smaller, direct voter events in early primary states.

Tulsa County reserve deputy Robert Bates has been placed on administrative leave after inadvertently shooting and killing suspect Eric Courtney Harris during an arrest. Police state that Bates, who was attempting to use a Taser, mistakenly discharged his service weapon, resulting in the suspect's death. The incident occurred during a pursuit involving a violent crimes task force, and an investigation is currently underway to determine the exact circumstances.

Mike Pence's signing of Indiana's religious freedom law was a calculated move to secure his standing as a conservative contender for the 2016 Republican presidential nomination, despite significant backlash from business leaders and the public. The decision highlights a growing rift within the GOP, forcing potential candidates like Jeb Bush and Ted Cruz to defend the measure and pushing the entire primary field further to the right on LGBT issues. Walmart's opposition to a controversial religious freedom law in Arkansas has positioned the retailer as a bellwether for shifting public opinion on social and economic issues. By advocating for LGBTQ+ protections and wage increases, the company is moving toward more progressive stances that reflect its diverse consumer base. This evolution suggests a potential shift in political influence, prompting some Republicans to urge the party to adopt more moderate policies to better represent the middle class.

In a broad bipartisan vote, the Senate passed a Medicare reform bill to ensure a permanent solution for the "doc fix" and a two-year extension of a children's health insurance program.

The bill, which has already passed the House, is now expected to be signed by President Barack Obama.

The legislation aims to stabilize Medicare provider payments and prevent the immediate expiration of temporary funding cuts to physicians.

Following his performance at Coachella, Jack White announced he will take a hiatus from touring after a brief, five-state acoustic tour. These unannounced shows will feature a small quartet and will be sold for only $3 at the venue on a first-come, first-served basis.

A massive four-alarm fire broke out Friday morning at the General Electric Appliance Park in Louisville, Kentucky, sending thick smoke over the area. While the cause of the blaze remains unknown, authorities reported that there were no injuries or trapped individuals.

Brett McGurk, the Obama administration’s point man on ISIS, described the terror group as a historically unprecedented threat that has placed the U.S. in "uncharted territory" due to the massive influx of foreign fighters. An American citizen was shot and wounded in Karachi, Pakistan, while driving from the medical school where she works. Debra Lobo, a 55-year-old vice principal, was targeted by two assailants on a motorcycle who threw pamphlets stating "America should be burnt."

Ursula Ward delivered an emotional statement in court following the conviction of Aaron Hernandez, describing her son Odin Lloyd as the "backbone of the family" and the man who kept his sisters together. Lloyd, a 27-year-old landscaping worker and former semi-pro football player, was killed in 2013, and his mother expressed that while she misses him deeply, she finds strength in the belief she will see him again. The sentencing brings closure to a case that has deeply affected Lloyd's family, who remember him as a hard worker and devoted relative.

Adelma Cifuentes’ harrowing experience with domestic abuse highlights the broader epidemic of gender-based violence in Guatemala, where femicide rates are among the highest in the world. This crisis is fueled by a legacy of impunity from the country’s civil war, entrenched misogyny, and the influence of organized crime, resulting in a system where nearly 98% of femicide cases go unpunished.

An Amnesty International report is calling for urgent action to protect women's rights activists in Afghanistan following a rise in targeted attacks and violence. The report highlights how activists face persecution from the Taliban, warlords, and government officials, often with little legal accountability for perpetrators. Despite these life-threatening risks, women continue to demonstrate remarkable resilience and solidarity in their fight for human rights.

Five Americans who were exposed to Ebola in Sierra Leone were released from an Omaha hospital after three weeks of monitoring, with one discharged for a heart-related issue. The group, who are clinicians for Partners in Health, had contact with an infected colleague at the NIH but none developed the virus. As the CDC expects to release the last of 17 monitored patients by Thursday, the outbreak has killed over 10,000 people in West Africa since December 2013.

University of Kentucky guard Andrew Harrison apologized for saying "F**k that (N-word)" about teammate Frank Kaminsky during a postgame press conference. Harrison claimed his comment was "in jest" and meant no disrespect to Kaminsky, who is white, while noting he is black. Following the backlash, Harrison tweeted an apology, stating he immediately reached out to Kaminsky to apologize after realizing how the comment could be perceived. Kaminsky said he was "over it" and noted "Nothing needs to be made out of it."

authorities in North Carolina have opened a hate crime investigation after the fatal shooting of Ron Lane, a gay and white employee at Wayne Community College. The suspect, Kenneth Morgan Stancil III, was arrested in Florida after fleeing the scene and was found sleeping on a beach with a knife. Lane’s relatives stated that he was gay, while investigators examine whether Stancil was affiliated with a white supremacist gang. Stancil, who had been dismissed from a work-study program earlier in March, allegedly shot Lane with a shotgun before fleeing on a motorcycle.

Following reports from two magazines claiming they have seen a video showing the final moments of Germanwings Flight 9525, French investigators and officials have denied the existence of such footage.

The lead prosecutor and the French Gendarmerie stated that no such video has been used in the investigation and that any discovered footage must be sent to specialized technicians for analysis. While media editors maintain the footage is real, officials emphasized that the cell phones recovered from the crash site have not yet been processed by the criminal research institute.

A New Jersey auction house removed items from its April 17 event after an uproar from the public.
